topic: Co-axial and counter rotating propellers, forces acting on propeller
syllabus_extract: Co-axial and counter rotating propellers, forces acting on propeller. Constant Speed Unit (CSU)
specific_objectives: 12.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to describe the various types of propellers, principles of operation and pitch change mechanisms.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of PPT diagrams; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation
intro_questions: What is the primary function of a propeller?
Name two types of propellers based on rotation direction.

development.content:
Co-axial propeller configuration
Counter rotating propeller system
Advantages of counter rotation
Forces acting on propeller blades
Blade element momentum theory

Constant Speed Unit (CSU) operation
Governor mechanism function
Pitch change mechanisms
Hydraulic vs mechanical control
CSU response to throttle changes

Propeller efficiency factors
Torque effect mitigation
Vibration causes and solutions
CSU maintenance basics
Operational limitations

summary_questions: Explain how counter rotation reduces torque effect.
Describe the role of the CSU in maintaining constant RPM.
List three forces acting on a propeller blade.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the operational advantages of co-axial propellers versus conventional single propellers, referencing LP 02.
